author: Ifmyante
text:
If you're not one to simply trade on the touch of a zone, but would rather wait for confirmation that price has rejected, there are some brilliant PA patterns you can look for before you enter a trade.

The best ones we'll cover involve an Engulf

Simply put, an engulf involves price making a lower low on reaction to Supply, or higher high from Demand This is a very powerful sign that price is on the turn. They say that a trend is a succession of LL's and HH's, or vice versa, so if you get a Lower Low from Supply, it's a great first sign that the uptrend may be over, and of course flip the scenario for an HH from Demand.

If you didn't have the patience to wait for that engulf, see the Lower timeframe for another lovely engulf showing the way much earlier!

author: Mike1
text: I certainly wanted to post a chart but I wasn't around my computer; now I am and I attached this one, where I added a few comments. My understanding so far is this: we wait for a PAZ to form in a Supply zone (opposite for longs). The area below the PAZ is a FL, a small demand zone that temporary keeps the price inside the PAZ (flag). Then, when FL gets engulfed, we enter short at the first RT into the engulfing candle. I'm gonna scrap then all my blurry ideas about these engulfings: pinbars, first classic engulfing candle, opposite direction momentum (WRB) candles... Should we skip it if there is no clear pole coming into the Supply zone or there are messy, hard to define PAZes? Thanks a lot!

author: Harry
text:
@ L_P, i agree with how you marked these series of smaller swings as a flag.

@ Mike1, this is a 2-part example. on the 1st chart IF show how we could wait for a confirmed entry (wait for a base engulf first and return to a QM level for example) on the 2nd chart he shows how a quicker (with confirmation) entry could have been after the engulf of the FL. your comments about it are correct, holds the flagging area up and needs to be engulfed to start looking for shorts. the truth is it didnt give such great chances to enter after the engulf, so yes was a hard one to take (for me).

i dont know if you have read the article about the Flag Limit in Markepedia yet, readthemarket.com/index.php/education/ma...edia/485-flag-limits the discussion thread is here readthemarket.com/index.php/forum/tradin...ons/1628-flag-limits

btw, see if you can draw this top part of the flag as i suggested (like IF did in his line diagram above) and find where you could have entered according to engulfs only.
